Goals: - Make the result of an operation reviewable from its report alone.
- Make the verification -- the bounding-box comparison above all -- automatic rather than a step an agent may skip.
- Give the operator a way to navigate the chain of operations and see what each one changed.
- Keep the contract agent-agnostic: one command, one JSON report, no runtime-specific integration.
- Keep every generated artefact under work/, so a public repository never carries private geometry.
Key product decisions: - One envelope, two payloads: a transform reports before and after, an inspection reports findings. Settled in `adr_001_operation_report_format`.

- The bounding-box comparison is computed by the report writer, not by the operation, because it is the check that caught every failure in the delivered chain while the manifold checks passed throughout. A verification an agent can forget is not a verification.
- What was not checked is stated as a warning code, so an agent can act on it and a reader is never left assuming.
- A failed operation is a branch of the history, kept and rendered, not a run to discard. `run_007` records three failed approaches, and they carry most of that runbook's value.
- Lineage lives in the files: a parent report id and wiki-style document references, no index and no database. A report stays understandable opened alone, years later, without the tool that wrote it.
- Reports are records and artefacts are files. Pruning deletes heavy artefacts and never the record of what was done.
Overview: Turns each headless 3D operation into a self-describing unit of work: one command runs it, one report records what it did and how that was verified, and one local viewer makes the chain readable without opening the 3D application. The measurement discipline the runbooks describe becomes something the tooling produces by default rather than something the operator has to remember.

- One JSON envelope per operation, written by a single helper, carrying what was measured, what it was measured against, and what was not checked -- so a result can be reviewed, and a chain of results navigated, from the reports alone.
References: - Prior art: `transformation-report.json` in the cm-sim printable-preparation flow (schema_version, source fingerprint, warning codes)
- The check the format makes mandatory: `run_006_turn_a_cad_assembly_into_a_printable_solid`, "compare the output bounding box against the source"
- The branching history this format must keep: `run_007_hollow_a_printable_body_for_electronics`, three failed approaches

Overview: - The viewer never runs an operation. Every action it offers -- run, re-run, branch, prune, re-render, open in Blender -- is presented as the exact command that does it, ready to copy, and the operator or the agent runs it themselves.
References: - The command this decision points to: `item_002_run_one_named_operation_from_a_single_agent_agnostic_command`

ai_context.keywords: operation report, bounding-box comparison, headless Blender, local viewer, agent-agnostic command
ai_context.skip when: Working on the geometry of one procedure -- the runbooks in logics/runbook/ hold that, not this request.
ai_context.summary: Each headless operation writes a report carrying its measurements and its bounding-box comparison, one command runs it whatever agent is driving, and a local viewer makes the chain readable without opening Blender.
ai_context.use when: Deciding how an operation records what it did, how it is invoked, or how its result is reviewed.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Every operation writes one report file under work/ops/ carrying its identifier, the script that ran, the input file, the output file, the measurements before and after, and the paths of any renders it produced.
- AC2: Each report states the output bounding box against the input bounding box, per axis, in millimetres, together with the axes that moved.
- AC3: The seven pipeline steps and tools/scan_defects.py write a report through the same helper, so no operation reports in a format of its own.
- AC4: A single command runs one named operation and writes its report, with no argument that depends on the agent runtime driving it.
- AC5: A local viewer lists the operations in execution order and, for a selected one, shows its measurements, its bounding-box comparison and its renders.
- AC6: The viewer reads only the report files. Opening it requires no Blender process, no build step and no network access.
Needs: - Reviewing what an operation did must not require opening Blender and navigating to the affected geometry by hand.
- Every operation must leave behind the measurements that verify it, not only its output file.
- The chain of operations that produced a result must be readable in order, with what changed at each step.
- Failed attempts must survive: three failed approaches are recorded in run_007 and they carry most of that runbook's value.
- The generated artefacts must be prunable without erasing the record of what was done, because a blend weighs 200 MB and a report a few kilobytes.

- Two states of the same geometry must be comparable side by side, not only through their numbers: a 30 mm voxel destroys the detail of a part while the volume moves by 3% and every topology check stays green.

ai_context.keywords: operation report, report writer, bounding-box delta, work/ops, failure report
ai_context.skip when: Deciding how an operation is invoked (item_002) or displayed (item_003).
ai_context.summary: One JSON report per operation under work/ops/, written by a single helper, carrying counts, bounding boxes before and after, the per-axis delta, render paths, and a failure path that still reports.
ai_context.use when: Changing what an operation records, or adding an operation that must report like the others.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Running any converted operation leaves exactly one report file under work/ops/, named with its execution order and operation name.
- AC2: The report states the bounding box before and after in millimetres and names the axes that moved, matching what the script prints.
- AC3: An operation raising an exception still leaves a report whose status is failed and which carries the error text.
- AC4: The report writer is the only place a report is written; no script serialises one of its own.
- AC5: An inspection script, which has no output file, produces a valid report of kind inspection carrying its findings.
- AC6: A measurement an operation did not take is null in the report, distinguishable from a measured zero.
Problem: - Each script prints its measurements to stdout and they are lost when the terminal scrolls.

- Twelve scripts exist, and they are not of one kind: seven transform a file, five only measure and produce no output at all. A format built around an input and an output cannot describe the second kind.
- Nothing links an output file to the operation, the input and the settings that produced it.
- The bounding-box comparison is described in the runbooks as the check that caught every failure, but it is computed by hand, differently, in each script.

ai_context.summary: One command that resolves the Blender binary, runs a named operation headless on a target file, refuses to write to work/in/, and prints the report path.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: One command runs a named operation on a given file and prints the path of the report it wrote.
- AC2: The same command works unchanged whether it is typed by hand or run by an agent; nothing in its interface depends on the runtime.
- AC3: Pointing the command at a file under work/in/ is refused with a message naming what to do instead.
- AC4: The Blender binary comes from an environment variable when set, and from the documented default otherwise.
Problem: - Running an operation today means knowing the Blender binary path, the -b and -P flags, which file to open and which script to pass.
- That invocation is what every agent has to reconstruct, and it is where a wrong file or a missing copy silently ruins the work.
- Nothing enforces that an operation runs on a copy rather than on a source under work/in/.

ai_context.keywords: local viewer, operation timeline, verification renders, static page, no build step
ai_context.skip when: Anything that runs or edits geometry -- the viewer only reads reports.
ai_context.summary: A static local page over work/ops/: operations in execution order, and for one of them its measurements, its per-axis bounding-box comparison and its renders side by side.
ai_context.use when: Changing how an operator reviews what an operation did.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: Opening the viewer with reports present renders them as a top-down DAG in execution order, with each node's status.
- AC5: Two operations sharing a parent are shown as siblings, and a failed one is kept in the tree rather than hidden.
- AC6: The selected operation's renders are shown large, one per canonical direction, with the path and camera of the one displayed.
- AC7: No menu entry runs anything: each shows the command that performs the action.
- AC2: Selecting an operation shows its measurements, its per-axis bounding-box comparison and its renders on one page.
- AC3: The viewer opens with no Blender process running, no build step and no network access.
Problem: - Reviewing an operation means reopening Blender and navigating to the affected geometry, which is slow enough that the review is skipped.
- The measurements and the renders exist separately, so the render is read on its own -- exactly the mistake the runbooks warn against.
- There is no view of the chain: which operation ran before this one, and what it changed.
- The history is a tree, not a line: `run_007` records three failed approaches before the one that worked, and a flat list cannot show that they were siblings.
